title: View spec, view/0
description: A view described once, in catalog names. It carries no sizes and no breakpoints; the container it lands in decides presentation.

title.description: Shown by the container's frame, not drawn in the scene.

use.description: A preset name. Expands into layers. Ignored if layers is present. The library ships: line, bar-list, share-bar, grouped-bar, stacked-bar, stacked-area, pie, donut, pie-semi-circle, gauge, heatmap, funnel, box-plot, error-bars, waterfall, candlestick, fan, dumbbell, bullet. A custom mark's package registers the presets that draw it, in code, with registerPreset(): the geo package registers choropleth and symbol-map, and the flow package registers sankey. A code base may also hand resolve() a library of its own. So this is not an enum: resolve() checks the name against the library and then the registry, and its error lists the presets there are.

keep.description: Parts a container may not drop.

allOf.description: A dimension needs something to draw it with: layers, or a preset.
A preset needs a dimension in query.by. The gauge takes none: it reads a metric against its catalog domain.

metrics.description: Catalog metric names. The first is the primary metric.

by.description: Zero, one or two catalog dimensions. With two, a layer must encode each: the second usually goes to color, or to the other axis of a grid of cells.

field.description: A dimension name, a metric name, a companion the result returns with one, written "<metric>@<suffix>", or a number (for a rule, on x or on y).

anyOf.description: The name of a custom mark registered in code. "geo" is one: one layer alone, with the dimension of region keys on x and a metric on color (a fill) or on size (a symbol). "link" is the other: one layer alone, with the source dimension on x, the target dimension on y and a metric on size. A schema cannot list those: resolve() checks the name against the registry, and its error lists the marks there are.

angle.description: For an arc: a metric. With a dimension on color each segment is its share of the total. With none the metric is read against its catalog domain.

radius.description: For an arc: the inner radius, as a share of the outer. 0.6 makes a donut.

size.description: A metric. A dot's size is one of a few steps, and the painter says how big each is.

x2.description: For a bar, a rule or an area with a field on x: its second end. The mark runs from the value on x to this one.

y2.description: For a bar, a rule or an area with a field on y: its second end. The mark runs from the value on y to this one.

series.description: "previous" draws the comparison companion of the metric. On a text layer in rows, "delta" says each row's change on the previous period, painted by the metric's polarity. Either needs "compare" in the query.

stack.description: On a layer split by color: each series starts where the one under it ends. "normalize" makes each a share of the whole, and "center" sets each stack half on either side of zero. A bar split by color with no stack sits beside its neighbours.

sweep.description: On an arc: the arcs run over the top half of the circle and not all the way round. The one layer field that is neither data nor role.

paint.description: A paint token, never a colour: series.1 to series.6, compare, rule, ink, ink.muted, delta. A layer with none takes series.1, so a second metric on the same plot wants "series.2". "delta" is the paint of the metric's change over the range: good or bad by its polarity, and the layer's own where there is no change to judge.
